abstracts.abstract: This paper presents a novel information-theoretic framework for adaptive filtering that fundamentally reconceptualizes signal processing in Riemannian manifold space. Unlike conventional approaches based on Euclidean geometry and mean-squared error minimization, the proposed framework employs the geometry of probability distributions to characterize the intrinsic structure of input data. We derive a family of adaptive algorithms by generalizing the classical steepest descent method to the manifold of covariance matrices, where the natural gradient replaces the ordinary gradient in parameter updates. The theoretical analysis demonstrates that the proposed Riemannian adaptive filtering (RAF) algorithm achieves superior performance in non-Euclidean signal spaces while maintaining computational tractability. Convergence properties are rigorously established using geodesic convexity theory, proving almost sure convergence under mild conditions. Furthermore, we show that classical LMS and RLS algorithms emerge as special cases of this unified framework. Simulation results on non-stationary channel equalization and time-varying spectral tracking validate the theoretical findings, revealing significant gains in tracking performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. This paradigm shift provides researchers with a powerful tool for addressing signal processing challenges where data exhibits inherent geometric structure.

This paper presents an enhanced sparse adaptive filtering algorithm that significantly improves parameter estimation accuracy for systems exhibiting sparse impulse responses. Traditional proportionate-type algorithms, while effective for sparse systems, suffer from suboptimal performance when the sparsity level varies dynamically. The proposed method incorporates a novel adaptive sparsity-aware step-size mechanism that automatically adjusts the learning rate according to the estimated sparsity of the unknown system at each iteration. Specifically, we introduce a sparsity measure based on the l1-norm of the coefficient vector and develop a mixed l2/l1 norm penalized cost function that promotes sparse solutions. The convergence analysis is conducted using energy conservation arguments, establishing bounds on the steady-state excess mean-squared error that explicitly account for the sparsity level. Analytical results reveal that the proposed sparsity-aware proportionate normalized LMS (SA-PNLMS) algorithm achieves up to 15 dB performance improvement over conventional PNLMS in highly sparse scenarios while maintaining competitive performance for dispersive channels. Complexity analysis shows that the computational overhead is negligible compared to existing proportionate methods. The algorithm's robustness to sparsity misestimation is demonstrated through comprehensive simulations involving acoustic echo cancellation and network echo compensation.

This paper introduces a novel distributed adaptive processing architecture for heterogeneous sensor networks that fundamentally transforms array signal processing in IoT environments. Conventional centralized processing systems suffer from excessive communication overhead and vulnerability to single-point failures, which severely limit their applicability in large-scale deployments. The proposed architecture employs a hybrid gossip-consensus protocol that enables nodes to collaborate efficiently without requiring a fusion center, achieving robust and scalable direction-of-arrival estimation. The system incorporates novel adaptive beamforming modules at each sensor node, enabling real-time interference suppression while maintaining low-power operation suitable for battery-powered devices. We present a comprehensive hardware implementation using software-defined radio platforms integrated with low-complexity processing units, demonstrating practical feasibility for frequencies from 400 MHz to 6 GHz. The network synchronization mechanism ensures coherent signal combination across distributed nodes while tolerating asynchronous arrivals. Experimental validation in indoor and outdoor environments demonstrates that the proposed system achieves comparable localization accuracy to centralized approaches while reducing communication bandwidth by 85%. This architecture enables new applications in smart cities, environmental monitoring, and emergency response systems where robust distributed sensing is essential.

This paper presents an improved real-time fetal electrocardiogram (FECG) extraction system that significantly advances the state-of-the-art in biomedical signal processing for prenatal monitoring. Existing methods struggle to reliably separate the weak fetal cardiac signal from strong maternal interference and measurement noise, particularly during ambulatory monitoring. The proposed system integrates a novel multi-channel adaptive noise canceler with a deep neural network-based post-processor that learns to refine the adaptive filter output by exploiting spatial correlations across abdominal electrode arrays. The architecture employs a recursive least-squares adaptive core for real-time operation, enhanced with a sparsity-promoting regularization term that exploits the quasi-periodic nature of cardiac signals. Hardware implementation utilizes a low-power ARM processor with optimized fixed-point arithmetic, achieving continuous processing at 500 Hz sampling rate with latency under 50 ms. Clinical validation on a dataset of 150 recordings from 75 patients demonstrates that the proposed system improves maternal cancellation ratio by 12 dB compared to our previous implementation and achieves reliable fetal R-peak detection in 94% of cases. The system successfully operates in real-time on battery-powered wearable devices, enabling extended continuous monitoring that was previously impractical. This work provides clinicians with a practical tool for improved prenatal cardiac assessment.
